title: MLOps — Retrain Only with a Defined Trigger
key_insight: Triggers may use enough new labeled data, measured drift, performance decay, or a deliberate product change. Every run still needs data validation and comparison gates.
body:
## Retrain Only with a Defined Trigger

A scheduled retraining job runs weekly even when data is broken. Automation repeats the damage faster.

Triggers may use enough new labeled data, measured drift, performance decay, or a deliberate product change. Every run still needs data validation and comparison gates.

Use a champion-challenger process: the candidate must beat the current model on agreed slices without breaking safety or operational limits.
common_mistakes: MLOps means copying the newest model file into production.
Scheduled retraining makes data validation unnecessary.
A model name alone proves which data produced it.
mini_exercise: Draw “Retrain Only with a Defined Trigger” as three labeled steps, then explain the decision at each step.
real_world_usage: Models and their data change, so production quality depends on lifecycle controls beyond ordinary code deployment.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Retrain Only with a Defined Trigger,” explain MLOps without assuming the listener knows AI engineering.
